Nodes: ILLUSION_MOVE (initial) -> SWIPE_MOVE -> BRANCH; SWIPE_RANDOM_MOVE -> HEADBUTT_MOVE -> SWIPE_MOVE. BRANCH is added SWIPE_RANDOM first then HEADBUTT (Fogmog.cs:46-47), both overload #6 (`MoveRepeatType, Func<float>`) so there is no integer to misread at all: CannotRepeat, weights 0.4f and 0.6f. fogmog.py:82-83 adds them in the same order with the same weights and repeat type. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py machine`, seeds b01-b03, 40 turns): identical sequences and identical MonsterAi draw counts (17/17, 18/18, 16/16) -- the draw count is below 40 precisely because SWIPE_RANDOM -> HEADBUTT -> SWIPE is a deterministic leg.

guards.what: Range-bound convention on the initial-HP roll: Rng.NextInt(min, max) is max-EXCLUSIVE (Rng.cs:101-109) where Python's random.randint(a, b) INCLUDES b
guards.rationale: Checked as a convention, not just as constants. The GAME's range is [MinInitialHp, MaxInitialHp] INCLUSIVE, because Creature.SetUniqueMonsterHpValue compensates for the exclusive bound explicitly: `int num = Monster.MaxInitialHp + 1` (Creature.cs:378) feeds BOTH `Enumerable.Range(minInitialHp, num - minInitialHp)` (Creature.cs:379) and the fallback `rng.NextInt(minInitialHp, num)` (Creature.cs:383). The sim's parity port matches on both arms: `candidates = [v for v in range(lo, hi + 1) ...]` picked with `niche.next_int_range(0, len(candidates))`, fallback `niche.next_int_range(lo, hi + 1)` (combat.py:224-243), and `next_int_range` is itself max-exclusive (rng.py:182-186) -- so the two `+ 1`s land exactly where C# puts them. This unit's MaxInitialHp is `=> MinInitialHp`, so the range is the single value 74 and no endpoint can be lost; the check is recorded anyway because an off-by-one would turn a one-element candidate list into an empty one and change which ARM of SetUniqueMonsterHpValue runs (NextItem vs NextInt), which is a stream-position difference even when the HP is identical. Executed (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b01.py hprange`, 400 seeded combats per unit): declared [74,74], observed [74,74], and the observed set is exactly the full inclusive range, so the top endpoint 74 does occur. All 15 units of this batch pass. NOTE the legacy (non-parity) path is also right by a different route: Monster.__init__'s `rng.randint(self.min_hp, self.max_hp)` (monsters/base.py:78) is inclusive on both ends, matching the game's inclusive range, and in parity mode it is overwritten before anything reads it. Rule 7: Creature.cs, Rng.cs, sts2_rl/combat.py and sts2_rl/rng.py are hashed in extra_sources.
